Today, Amazon's subsidiary Ring announced the launch of its first smart door lock, addressing a problem that has long plagued many smart lock users: dead batteries. Ring has an ingenious solution to avoid this issue, and the product will be released in the first quarter of 2027. In addition, the company also announced several new security cameras with improved low-light performance.

Ring Smart Door Lock

The concept of a smart door lock is not new, but Ring wants to solve the problem of smart lock battery depletion. To prevent you from being locked out at an inconvenient time, the Ring Smart Door Lock allows you to turn the manual knob on the lock a few times, using the energy generated to briefly power the lock, so you can immediately unlock the door and get back home.

The Ring Smart Door Lock has everything you would expect from a smart door lock. You can unlock it with a fingerprint, a touch-sensitive numeric keypad, or via the Ring app on your phone.

The Ring app also offers a number of features, including remotely viewing and locking the door, as well as setting recurring or time-limited access for family members or other visitors. It can also integrate with Amazon Echo and other Ring doorbells and cameras you may own.

The door lock is available in three colours: black, silver and brass, and requires no additional wiring. It will go on sale early next year for US$249. You can learn more about it here.

All-New 4K Cameras

In addition to its first smart door lock, Ring has also launched several 4K cameras that support the new Retinal Vision 4K standard, meaning you'll enjoy better low-light footage and accurate colours. All products are available for pre-order or purchase starting today:

  • Outdoor Cam 4K Plus: 140° wide-angle lens, offering multiple power options including battery, plug-in, wired and Power over Ethernet — US$149.99 on Amazon, learn more here
  • Floodlight Cam 4K Plus: powerful floodlight, supports 24-hour continuous recording and smart detection, wired connection — US$219.99 on Amazon, learn more here
  • Spotlight Cam 4K Plus: 550-lumen spotlight, 140° wide-angle lens, available in battery, plug-in and solar power configurations — US$199.99 on Amazon, learn more here
  • Indoor Cam 4K: Ring's first 4K indoor camera, supports dual-band Wi-Fi 6, with a 115° field of view — US$99.99 on Amazon, learn more here

Ring has also launched the new Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K, priced at US$69.99, offering 360° panoramic rotating coverage at a more affordable price. It can track motion and has a built-in privacy cover. Learn more here.
